paragraphs.text: Samanta Chandrasekhar, also known as Pathani Samanta, was an astronomer associated with Khandapada in Odisha. His work combined observation and calculation within the traditional Sanskrit astronomical tradition. He recorded his studies in the Siddhanta Darpana.

The indexed abstract of Naik and Satpathy’s paper describes observations made with instruments he fabricated himself and contributions to observation, calculation, instrumentation and astronomical models. This draft does not independently test the accuracy of those calculations.

sections.title: The book that carried the work forward

paragraphs.text: The Siddhanta Darpana presents astronomical work in Sanskrit verse. The Orissa Review account places it in conversation with earlier works, including the Surya Siddhanta and Siddhanta Siromani.

Odia Bibhaba’s catalogue identifies an original publication dated 1899 and provides links to Sanskrit editions, Odia, Hindi and English translations, and later studies. These are starting points for reading the work itself, beyond retellings of its author’s life.

The sources do not agree on his birth date. The 1998 paper’s abstract and the Odia Bibhaba catalogue give the lifespan as 1835–1904; the 2007 Orissa Review article gives 11 January 1836 as his birth date. We leave the discrepancy open rather than silently harmonizing it.

Claims about exact predictive accuracy need comparison with the original calculations and specialist review. This entry therefore focuses on the documented work and available source trail, without repeating claims of unrivalled scientific achievement.
